questions.question: How can I change or replace one of the built-in theme's UI pieces without forking the whole theme?

answer.content:
{"answer": "The evidence shows built-in UI pieces are shipped as individual components under per-component `src/theme/<Name>/...` paths inside the theme packages — e.g. `packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/DocTagDocListPage/index.tsx`, `packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/BlogPostItem/Header/Info/index.tsx`, and `packages/docusaurus-theme-search-algolia/src/theme/SearchPage/index.tsx` (the summary for `SearchPage` explicitly calls it "the swizzled Algolia full-page search results component"). So each UI piece is a separately addressable component, not one monolithic theme file.

However, the actual mechanism for changing/replacing one of these pieces without forking (swizzle command, wrapping/ejecting, theme component aliasing, `@theme/...` resolution) is **not in the evidence** — the atlas search returned only plurals/utilities/options modules, nothing documenting that workflow. What the evidence does give you about those pieces once you touch them:

- Shared theme hooks live in `@docusaurus/theme-common` and are reused by theme components: `usePluralForm` (`packages/docusaurus-theme-common/src/utils/usePluralForm.ts`), `usePrevious` (`packages/docusaurus-theme-common/src/utils/reactUtils.tsx`), `useLocationChange` (`packages/docusaurus-theme-common/src/utils/useLocationChange.ts`), `useBlogPostsPlural` (`packages/docusaurus-theme-common/src/translations/blogTranslations.tsx`).
- Theme components call these via local helpers such as `useNDocsTaggedPlural`, `useReadingTimePlural`, `useDocumentsFoundPlural`.
- The search/algolia and classic containers are separate packages (`container:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic`, `container:packages-docusaurus-theme-search-algolia`), so a piece belongs to one theme package.

To answer the question fully, we'd need evidence on swizzling/theme component override rules — not present here.","citations":["component:packages-docusaurus-theme-search-algolia-src-theme-search-page-index-tsx","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-doc-tag-doc-list-page-index-tsx","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-blog-post-item-header-info-index-tsx","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-doc-tag-doc-list-page-index-tsx:use-n-docs-tagged-plural","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-blog-post-item-header-info-index-tsx:use-reading-time-plural","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-search-algolia-src-theme-search-page-index-tsx:use-documents-found-plural","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-utils-use-plural-form-ts:use-plural-form","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-utils-react-utils-tsx","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-utils-use-location-change-ts","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-translations-blog-translations-tsx","container:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic","container:packages-docusaurus-theme-common","container:packages-docusaurus-theme-search-algolia"]}

questions.question: What exactly happens when I snapshot the current documentation as a new release version?

answer.content:
{"answer":"The actual snapshot command itself (the `docs:version` CLI that copies files and rewrites `versions.json`) is **not in the evidence** — the atlas only surfaced how the resulting version is read back and rendered. What the evidence does show is the consumption side:

- `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/constants.ts` defines the names a new version interacts with: `CURRENT_VERSION_NAME` = `'current'`, `VERSIONS_JSON_FILE` = `'versions.json'`, and `VERSIONED_DOCS_DIR`.
- `readVersionNames` (`packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/versions/files.ts`) reads `versions.json` via `readVersionsFile`, prepends `'current'` when `includeCurrentVersion` is set and not already listed, and throws if the result is empty or if `disableVersioning` is used on a non-versioned site.
- `getVersionMetadataPaths` resolves each version's `sidebarFilePath`, `contentPath` and `contentPathLocalized`.
- `createVersionMetadata` (`packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/versions/version.ts`) then builds the runtime record: label, banner (`getDefaultVersionBanner`), badge, `noIndex`, `className`, `path`/`tagsPath` routes from `baseUrl` + `routeBasePath` + version path part, edit URLs, `isLast`, and route priority. `readVersionsMetadata` is the entry point that assembles these.
- Downstream, `website/src/pages/versions.tsx` (`Version`) lists `current`, the latest and past versions with release-notes links, and `website/docusaurus.config.ts` derives `getLastStableVersion`/`getNextVersionName` (`'Canary'`) from the version list.

Missing: the command that writes the snapshot (file copying, `versions.json` update, sidebar snapshot) — that code was not among the 15 matched sections.","citations":["component:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-constants-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-constants-ts:current-version-name","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-constants-ts:versions-json-file","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-constants-ts:versioned-docs-dir","component:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-files-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-files-ts:read-version-names","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-files-ts:read-versions-file","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-files-ts:get-version-metadata-paths","component:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-version-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-version-ts:create-version-metadata","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-version-ts:read-versions-metadata","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-versions-version-ts:get-default-version-banner","component:website-src-pages-versions-tsx","code:website-src-pages-versions-tsx:version","component:website-docusaurus-config-ts","code:website-docusaurus-config-ts:get-last-stable-version","code:website-docusaurus-config-ts:get-next-version-name"]}

questions.question: How does the left-hand navigation get built automatically from my folders, and how do I control the order?

answer.content:
{"answer":"The evidence only covers how sidebar *navigation* (prev/next pagination) is derived from sidebar items — the actual auto-generation of sidebars from your folders and any ordering control is **not in the evidence**.

What is covered:
- `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/docs.ts` — `addDocNavigation` calls `sidebarsUtils.getDocNavigation` per doc (with `displayed_sidebar` front matter and unlisted suppression) to attach prev/next links; `doProcessDocMetadata` derives each doc's slug, route and title.
- `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/sidebars/utils.ts` — `toNavigationLink` turns a `SidebarNavigationItem` (category or doc) into a title/permalink link; `collectSidebarsNavigations` / `SidebarNavigation` gather these across sidebars.
- `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/sidebars/types.ts` — `SidebarNavigationItem` = `SidebarItemDoc | SidebarItemCategoryWithLink`, the shape traversal produces.
- `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/categoryGeneratedIndex.ts` — `getCategoryGeneratedIndexMetadata` builds generated category index pages.

Missing from the evidence: the folder-scanning / `autogenerated` sidebars logic, and any position/ordering mechanism (e.g. front matter or filename-based ordering) that determines left-nav order. questions.question: Why does my production build fail because of a link to a page that doesn't exist, and can I make it only warn?

answer.content:
{"answer": "Your build fails because the per-locale build pipeline runs a broken-links check after bundling: `executeBrokenLinksCheck()` in `packages/docusaurus/src/commands/build/buildLocale.ts` decides the outcome based on the `onBrokenLinks` (and `onBrokenAnchors`) settings, so with the default severity a missing route is treated as fatal. You can downgrade it to a warning by setting `onBrokenLinks: 'warn'` in your site config — the check then reports via the logger's `warn` instead of failing the build.

- `packages/docusaurus/src/commands/build/buildLocale.ts` — `buildLocale()` orchestrates bundling → `executePluginsPostBuild()` → `executeBrokenLinksCheck()`, which is where severity (`onBrokenLinks` / `onBrokenAnchors`) is applied.
- `packages/docusaurus/src/server/brokenLinks.ts` — `getBrokenLinks()` collects per-page results from `getBrokenLinksForPage()`, producing `BrokenLink` entries (`link`, `resolvedLink`, `anchor`) that the build check reports on.
- `packages/docusaurus-logger/src/logger.ts` — `warn()` is what actually prints the yellow warning when severity is set to warn; `packages/docusaurus/src/commands/build/build.ts` (`build()` → `runBuildLocaleTask()` → `tryToBuildLocale()`) is where a thrown error would surface as a failed build.

Note: the exact accepted values/wording of the `onBrokenLinks` option are not in the evidence — the buildLocale summary only states that `executeBrokenLinksCheck()` "decides outcomes from `onBrokenLinks` and `onBrokenAnchors`". Separately, broken *markdown* links are handled earlier in `packages/docusaurus-mdx-loader/src/remark/transformLinks/index.ts` (`processLinkNode` → `context.onBrokenMarkdownLinks`), which is a different (also severity-configurable) path.", "citations": ["component:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-locale-ts", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-locale-ts:execute-broken-links-check", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-locale-ts:build-locale", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-locale-ts:execute-plugins-post-build", "component:packages-docusaurus-src-server-broken-links-ts", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-broken-links-ts:get-broken-links", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-broken-links-ts:get-broken-links-for-page", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-broken-links-ts:broken-link", "component:packages-docusaurus-logger-src-logger-ts", "code:packages-docusaurus-logger-src-logger-ts:warn-3", "component:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-ts", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-ts:build", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-ts:run-build-locale-task", "code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-build-build-ts:try-to-build-locale", "component:packages-docusaurus-mdx-loader-src-remark-transform-links-index-ts", "code:packages-docusaurus-mdx-loader-src-remark-transform-links-index-ts:process-link-node"]}

questions.question: How does the blog decide how much of a post to show on the list page?

answer.content: {"answer":"Two separate decisions: *how much text* of each post is shown is decided at build time by truncation markers in the source, and *how many posts* per list page is decided by `postsPerPage` pagination. Posts without a truncation marker are flagged by `reportUntruncatedBlogPosts`, so they effectively render in full on the list (with a warning to the user).","citations":["code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-blog-src-blog-utils-ts:report-untruncated-blog-posts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-blog-src-blog-utils-ts:paginate-blog-posts","component:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-blog-src-blog-utils-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-blog-src-options-ts:default-options","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-blog-list-page-index-tsx:blog-list-page-content"],"answer2":""}

questions.question: What runs when someone creates a brand-new site from the starter templates?

answer.content:
{"answer":"Scaffolding runs through `create-docusaurus`'s `init()` in `packages/create-docusaurus/src/index.ts`, which turns CLI flags/prompts into a new site directory: it resolves language, package manager, and template source, then copies the chosen template files into place.

- `createTemplateChoices` (`packages/create-docusaurus/src/index.ts`) builds the template menu; `getSiteName` asks for/validates the directory name.
- `createTemplateSource` resolves `Source` — either a bundled `Template` (with `type: 'template'` and `language`), a `git` URL, or `local` — and exits if a TypeScript variant is requested but the template has no `tsVariantPath` (see `Template`/`Source` in `packages/create-docusaurus/src/constants.ts`).
- `Template.path`/`tsVariantPath` point at `packages/create-docusaurus/templates/classic-typescript`, which is what gets copied: `docusaurus.config.ts` (`config`), `sidebars.ts` (`sidebars`, autogenerated sidebar), `src/pages/index.tsx` (`Home`, `HomepageHeader`) and `src/components/HomepageFeatures/index.tsx` (`FeatureList`, `Feature`). These are placeholder content (`title: 'My Site'`).
- Side effects afterwards: `runGitCloneCommand`/`runCommand` (`packages/create-docusaurus/src/commands.ts`) for git sources, `runPackageManagerInstallCommand` to install deps, `siteNameToPackageName` + `updatePkg` (`packages/create-docusaurus/src/utils.ts`) to fix the manifest, then `printPackageManagerHelp` prints `cd`/start instructions.

Not in the evidence: the exact file-copy mechanics inside `init()` (e.g. shared-template merge/renames) — only the summary states files are copied into place. Also unrelated: the `start`/dev-server code in `packages/docusaurus/src/commands/start/*` runs later, when the user starts the generated site.","citations":["component:packages-create-docusaurus-src-index-ts","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-index-ts:create-template-source","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-index-ts:create-template-choices","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-index-ts:get-site-name","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-constants-ts:template","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-constants-ts:source","container:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-docusaurus-config-ts:config","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-sidebars-ts:sidebars","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-src-pages-index-tsx:home","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-src-pages-index-tsx:homepage-header","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-src-components-homepage-features-index-tsx:feature-list","code:packages-create-docusaurus-templates-classic-typescript-src-components-homepage-features-index-tsx:feature","component:packages-create-docusaurus-src-commands-ts","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-commands-ts:run-git-clone-command","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-commands-ts:run-command","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-commands-ts:run-package-manager-install-command","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-utils-ts:site-name-to-package-name","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-utils-ts:update-pkg","code:packages-create-docusaurus-src-utils-ts:print-package-manager-help"]}

questions.question: How is the 'Edit this page' link at the bottom of a doc put together?

answer.content:
{"answer":"The link is built by the `EditThisPage` theme component: it renders a `Link` to the `editUrl` prop with class `ThemeClassNames.common.editThisPage`, an `IconEdit` icon, and a `<Translate id="theme.common.editThisPage">Edit this page</Translate>` label.

- `packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/EditThisPage/index.tsx` — `EditThisPage` is the presentational piece; it does no URL construction itself, it just receives `editUrl`.
- `packages/docusaurus-utils/src/urlUtils.ts` — `getEditUrl(fileRelativePath, editUrl)` is what assembles the URL by joining the configured `editUrl` base with the doc's file path (forcing forward slashes).
- `packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/theme/EditMetaRow/index.tsx` — `EditMetaRow` is the row component that hosts the edit link alongside last-updated info at the page bottom.
- `packages/docusaurus-theme-common/src/utils/ThemeClassNames.ts` — `ThemeClassNames.common.editThisPage` supplies the stable `theme-edit-this-page` styling hook.

What's missing from the evidence: the caller that passes `editUrl` into `EditThisPage`/`EditMetaRow` (i.e. the DocItem footer/`useDocsSidebar`-adjacent wiring that pulls `metadata.editUrl` from the docs plugin). The docs plugin's `doProcessDocMetadata` in `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/docs.ts` is present in the results but its excerpt doesn't show editUrl derivation, so that step is unverified.","citations":["component:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-edit-this-page-index-tsx","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-edit-this-page-index-tsx:edit-this-page","component:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-url-utils-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-url-utils-ts:get-edit-url","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-edit-meta-row-index-tsx","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-classic-src-theme-edit-meta-row-index-tsx:edit-meta-row","component:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-utils-theme-class-names-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-common-src-utils-theme-class-names-ts:theme-class-names","component:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-docs-ts","code:packages-docusaurus-plugin-content-docs-src-docs-ts:do-process-doc-metadata"]}

questions.question: Which Node.js version do I need to run it?

answer.content:
{"answer": "The exact minimum Node.js version isn't stated in the evidence — no `engines` field or version-check code surfaced. What the codebase does show is how Node's version is detected at runtime and used for build targeting, which tells you nothing about a required minimum.

- `packages/docusaurus-utils/src/constants.ts` — `NODE_MAJOR_VERSION` and `NODE_MINOR_VERSION` parse `process.versions.node` at runtime (there's also `DOCUSAURUS_VERSION`, unrelated to Node). These are runtime introspection, not a requirement.
- `packages/docusaurus/src/webpack/server.ts` — `createServerConfig` uses those constants to set the webpack SSR `target: \`node${NODE_MAJOR_VERSION}.${NODE_MINOR_VERSION}\``, i.e. it targets whatever Node is currently running.
- `packages/docusaurus-faster/src/index.ts` — `getLastBrowserslistKnownNodeVersion` falls back to `'22.0.0'` under `bundlerName: 'rspack'` (clamped by `getMinVersion`), but this is a browserslist target query for bundling, not a supported-Node floor.

So the missing piece is the declared requirement itself: a `engines.node` constraint or an explicit version check/guard is not in the evidence. To answer definitively, look at the root/package `package.json` `engines` field, which the atlas search didn't return.","citations":["code:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-constants-ts:node-major-version","code:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-constants-ts:node-minor-version","code:packages-docusaurus-src-webpack-server-ts:create-server-config","code:packages-docusaurus-faster-src-index-ts:get-last-browserslist-known-node-version","code:packages-docusaurus-faster-src-index-ts:get-min-version","component:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-constants-ts","component:packages-docusaurus-faster-src-index-ts"]}

questions.question: How are translations of the project's own documentation site managed and synced?

answer.content:
{"answer":"Translations of the docs site are synced through **Crowdin**: `website/waitForCrowdin.mjs` blocks the site build until no Crowdin project build is still running, so translated content is settled before it continues. It instantiates a `Translations` client with `CROWDIN_PERSONAL_TOKEN`, uses a hardcoded `projectId` (428890), and polls `hasBuildInProgress()` every 5s with a 5-minute ceiling.

- `website/waitForCrowdin.mjs` — `translations`, `projectId`, `hasBuildInProgress` (`component:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs`, `code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:translations`, `code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:project-id`, `code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:has-build-in-progress`)
- The translation files themselves are produced by `writeTranslations` in `packages/docusaurus/src/commands/writeTranslations.ts`, which loads the context/locales, calls `extractSiteSourceCodeTranslations`, applies plugin defaults and writes code translations plus per-plugin translation files via `writePluginTranslationFiles` (`code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-write-translations-ts:write-translations`, `code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-write-translations-ts:write-plugin-translation-files`, `code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-translations-translations-extractor-ts:extract-site-source-code-translations`).
- String extraction comes from `packages/docusaurus-babel/src/babelTranslationsExtractor.ts` (`extractSourceCodeAstTranslations`), gated by `isTranslatableSourceFile` in `packages/docusaurus-glob/src/translationUtils.ts`; output lands in `code.json` per `CODE_TRANSLATIONS_FILE_NAME` (`code:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-constants-ts:code-translations-file-name`), loaded at runtime by `loadSiteCodeTranslations` in `packages/docusaurus/src/server/translations/translations.ts`.
- Theme-level locale files are kept in sync by `packages/docusaurus-theme-translations/update.mjs` (`updateBaseFile`, `updateLocaleCodeTranslations`), and site-specific strings (navbar/footer, docs sidebars) come from `getTranslationFiles` in `packages/docusaurus-theme-classic/src/translations.ts` and `packages/docusaurus-plugin-content-docs/src/translations.ts`.

Not in the evidence: the actual Crowdin configuration (e.g. a crowdin config file or website npm scripts that invoke `waitForCrowdin`/upload-download steps), so the exact upload/download direction of the sync is unspecified here.","citations":["component:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs","code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:translations","code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:project-id","code:website-wait-for-crowdin-mjs:has-build-in-progress","code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-write-translations-ts:write-translations","code:packages-docusaurus-src-commands-write-translations-ts:write-plugin-translation-files","code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-translations-translations-extractor-ts:extract-site-source-code-translations","code:packages-docusaurus-babel-src-babel-translations-extractor-ts:extract-source-code-ast-translations","code:packages-docusaurus-glob-src-translation-utils-ts:is-translatable-source-file","code:packages-docusaurus-utils-src-constants-ts:code-translations-file-name","code:packages-docusaurus-src-server-translations-translations-ts:load-site-code-translations","code:packages-docusaurus-theme-translations-update-mjs:update-base-file","code:packages
